title: The 8237A DMA controller as a chip
covers: The 8237A DMA controller as a chip: reset state, end of process, transfer modes, transfer types, memory-to-memory, autoinitialize, priority and compressed timing

rows.text: Reset clears the Command, Request and Temporary registers and the first/last flip-flop.
Reset clears the Status register.
Reset sets the Mask register.
Following a Reset the device is in the Idle cycle.
EOP is a bidirectional signal that reports the completion of DMA services and lets an external signal terminate an active service.
The 8237A generates a pulse on the EOP line when the terminal count of any channel is reached.
On an internal EOP the service ends, the request is reset and, with Autoinitialize, the base registers are written to the current registers.
EOP sets the mask bit of the active channel unless it is programmed for Autoinitialize, in which case the mask bit remains unchanged.
During memory-to-memory transfers EOP is output when the TC for channel 1 occurs.
When the 8237A is in the Idle cycle and a non-masked channel requests a DMA service, it outputs HRQ and enters the Active cycle.
In Single Transfer mode the device is programmed to make one transfer only.
The address is decremented or incremented following each transfer.
The word count is decremented following each transfer.
When the word count rolls over from zero to FFFFH, a TC causes an Autoinitialize if the channel has been programmed to do so.
In Single Transfer mode DREQ must be held active until DACK becomes active; if it stays active, HRQ goes inactive and another single transfer follows.
In Block Transfer mode the device continues making transfers until a TC, caused by the word count going to FFFFH, is encountered.
In Block Transfer mode an external EOP also ends the service.
In Block Transfer mode DREQ need only be held active until DACK becomes active, and an Autoinitialization occurs at the end of the service if programmed.
In Demand Transfer mode the device continues making transfers until a TC is encountered or until DREQ goes inactive.
In Demand Transfer mode an external EOP also ends the service.
In Demand mode the intermediate address and word count stay in the current registers between services; only an EOP can cause an Autoinitialize.
Cascade mode connects more than one 8237A: the HRQ and HLDA of an added device go to the DREQ and DACK of a channel of the initial device.
In Cascade mode the 8237A responds to DREQ and DACK, all other outputs except HRQ are disabled, and the ready input is ignored.
Two additional devices can be cascaded into an initial device, forming two levels, and further devices into the second level channels, forming a third level.
Each of the three active transfer modes can perform three types of transfer: Read, Write and Verify.
Write transfers move data to memory by activating MEMW.
Write transfers take data from an I/O device by activating IOR.
Read transfers move data from memory by activating MEMR.
Read transfers send data to an I/O device by activating IOW.
Verify transfers generate addresses as in Read or Write and respond to EOP, but the memory and I/O control lines all remain inactive.
The memory-to-memory feature performs block moves of data from one memory address space to another.
Programming a bit in the Command register selects channels 0 and 1 for memory-to-memory transfer, started by the software DREQ for channel 0.
Memory-to-memory reads a byte from memory at the channel 0 address into the Temporary register.
Channel 1 then writes the Temporary register to memory at the address in its own Current Address register.
The channel 1 current word count is decremented; when it goes to FFFFH a TC is generated, causing an EOP output that terminates the service.
Channel 0 may be programmed to retain the same address for all transfers, which allows a single word to be written to a block of memory.
The 8237A responds to external EOP signals during memory-to-memory transfers; memory-to-memory operations can be detected as an active AEN with no DACK outputs.
A channel set to Autoinitialize by a Mode register bit has its Current Address and Word Count restored from the Base registers following EOP.
The base registers are loaded together with the current registers and unchanged throughout the service; the mask bit is not altered in Autoinitialize.
After Autoinitialize the channel is ready for another DMA service without CPU intervention as soon as a valid DREQ is detected.
To Autoinitialize both channels of a memory-to-memory transfer, both word counts should be programmed identically.
Fixed Priority ranks the channels by descending number: channel 0 is the highest priority and channel 3 the lowest.
After the recognition of one channel the others cannot interfere until its service is completed; then HRQ goes inactive and the 8237A waits for HLDA to go low.
In Rotating Priority the last channel to get service becomes the lowest priority channel with the others rotating accordingly.
With Rotating Priority in a single chip system any requesting device is guaranteed recognition after no more than three higher priority services.
In compressed timing state S3 is removed, so a transfer consists only of S2 and S4.
In compressed timing S1 states still occur when A8 to A15 need updating; the timing is in Figure 14.
The 8237A accepts programming from the host processor any time HLDA is inactive, even if HRQ is active; the host must keep programming and HLDA mutually exclusive.
A DMA request on an unmasked channel during programming can start a service after only one byte of an address register changes; disable the controller or mask the channel first.
After power-up it is suggested that all internal locations, especially the Mode registers, be loaded with some valid value, even for unused channels.
Reset executes m_status &= 0xf0, which clears bits 0 to 3 of the Status register and keeps bits 4 to 7.
A Verify transfer calls m_in_ior_cb in dma_read and m_in_memr_cb in dma_write, reading the I/O port and memory.
A new DmaController starts with the flip-flop clear and each new DmaChannel with the request flag clear; neither constructor stores a Command or Temporary register.
The channel constructor body stores no Idle cycle state.
ReachedTC sets tcount and calls the channel callback with DMA_REACHED_TC; its body has no EOP line.
At TC with autoinit set, DmaChannel::Read reloads currcnt and curraddr from the base values; its TC block stores no request flag.
In Verify mode DmaChannel::Write counts and advances curraddr without writing memory, but DmaChannel::Read returns 0 for a channel not in Read mode unless the program is DIAGNOSE.
A write at offset 0x08 stores nothing, so no Command bit selects memory-to-memory transfers.
A Mode write stores no bit 6 or 7 (a source comment questions it), so no Single mode is selected.
A Mode write stores no bit 6 or 7, so no Block mode is selected.
A Mode write stores no bit 6 or 7, so no Demand mode is selected.
A Mode write stores no bit 6 or 7, so no Cascade mode is selected.
A write at offset 0x08 does nothing, so no memory-to-memory selection exists.
A write at offset 0x08 stores nothing, so no Command bit starts a memory-to-memory sequence.
A write at offset 0x08 does nothing, so no priority scheme is selected.
A write at offset 0x08 does nothing, so no rotating priority is selected.
A write at offset 0x08 does nothing, so no compressed timing is selected.
A service starts with COMMAND_MEM_TO_MEM when any channel in Single mode has its request bit set; later lines set the current channel to 0 and then to 1.
Reset sets the current channel to -1, the last served channel to 3 and the HRQ state to -1, then calls set_hreq(0).
A transfer call on a masked channel logs a warning and moves no data, returning 0 units.
DmaChannel::Write stores the data from the buffer its caller passes in.
DmaChannel::Read hands the data it reads from memory back in the buffer its caller passes in.
A write at offset 0x08 stores nothing, so no Command bit starts a memory-to-memory sequence.
